blocks.content: The Moon is in synchronous rotation with Earth, always showing the same face to our planet.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and the fifth-largest satellite in the Solar System.
It is in synchronous rotation with Earth, completing both its rotation and revolution in approximately 27.3 days.
The lack of a significant atmosphere results in extreme temperature swings and a crater-marked surface.
Gravitational forces between Earth and the Moon generate the primary force behind ocean tides.

rows: Point in orbit closest to Earth
Point in orbit farthest from Earth

items: The scientific study of the Moon's physical features and geology is known as Selenology.
Light reflected from the Moon takes approximately 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth.
Due to tidal locking and libration, observers on Earth can see up to 59% of the lunar surface over time.
India's Chandrayaan-3 made history as the first mission to soft-land near the lunar South Pole.
